paper_metadata.title: Diagram-to-Circuit QNLP for Financial Sentiment Analysis

summary: The paper evaluates a QDisCoCirc-inspired gate-based QNLP model for financial sentiment classification using classical simulation of shallow IQP circuits (depth 4) and ~2.2×10^4 parameters. On the Financial PhraseBank (100% agreement subset, 2,263 sentences), the baseline quantum representation achieves test accuracy 0.696 and macro‑F1 0.551, far below the classical FinBERT baseline (accuracy 0.97, macro‑F1 0.95). Adding a classical Transformer over Bloch-vector sequences improves macro‑F1 to 0.5857 but remains purely classical.

experiments.description: Classical-simulation evaluation of a QDisCoCirc-inspired chunked diagram-to-circuit QNLP model for 3-class financial sentiment classification, using IQP-ansatz quantum circuits to generate Bloch-vector chunk representations and a mean-pooled sentence representation.

algorithm.variant: QDisCoCirc-inspired chunked diagram-to-circuit QNLP with IQP ansatz
algorithm.convergence_criteria: early stopping with burn-in of 2 epochs and maximum of 20 epochs

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Each chunk is mapped to a shallow quantum circuit; each chunk is represented as a single qubit and converted to a 2x2 density matrix via Bloch-vector extraction. Sentence representation is the uniform convex combination of valid chunk density matrices.
problem_formulation.objective_function: 3-way sentiment classification via softmax over class scores derived from normalized Hilbert-Schmidt similarity / cosine similarity between sentence representation and class label density matrices; trained with class-weighted cross-entropy.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Chunks whose types reduce to identity are excluded; class-specific thresholds are optimized on the dev set; class weighting by inverse class frequency.

problem_instance.description: Financial sentiment classification on the Financial PhraseBank dataset, using the 100%-agreement subset after preprocessing and chunking.

dataset_specification.description: 100%-agreement subset; 2,264 sentences originally, 2,263 remained after preprocessing; split into train/dev/test with 64%/16%/20% stratification preserving label distribution.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Rule-based vocabulary rewriting and chunk-boundary preservation: normalize copulas, numbers/units, upward/downward movement verbs, prepositions, finance-specific relative pronouns, compound prepositions, comparative expressions; merge passive constructions, fixed expressions, proper nouns, URLs/symbol sequences, as+past participle, to+verb, and sentence-initial discourse markers into stable chunks; CCG parsing with BobcatParser; sentences split into chunks of max 5 words; chunks with identity type excluded.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Train/dev/test split with macro-F1 on dev for model selection and threshold tuning; test accuracy and macro-F1 reported; class-specific thresholds optimized on dev set.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: BobcatParser CCG parsing; vocabulary rewriting; chunking; label prototype selection by farthest-first rule; threshold optimization on dev set.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Mean pooling of chunk density matrices; normalized Hilbert-Schmidt similarity / cosine similarity; softmax; class-specific thresholding; macro-F1 computation.

speedup_claims.caveats: No asymptotic or empirical quantum speedup is claimed; the paper explicitly states the evaluation relies on classical simulations.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Not specified; the paper only evaluates small simulated circuits with chunk-level single-qubit states and ~2.2×10^4 parameters.
limiting_factors: Entire experiment performed via classical simulation
Model accuracy (0.696 / macro-F1 0.551) far below classical FinBERT baseline (accuracy 0.97 / macro-F1 0.95)
No asymptotic complexity or speedup analysis provided
Quantum representation limited to single-qubit Bloch vectors per chunk
Hybrid architecture relies heavily on classical preprocessing and pooling

notes: No physical QPU is used; the paper states the evaluation relies on classical simulations, so hardware.type is simulator_other.

The paper says each chunk is prepared as a single qubit, but does not report a total qubit count for the full experiment; num_qubits is therefore not directly reported and cannot be reliably totaled from the text because chunking makes it sentence-dependent.
No asymptotic quantum/classical speedup analysis is provided; speedup_order is inferred as none_proven.
Table 2 reports FinBERT achieving accuracy 0.97 and macro-F1 0.95 compared with the proposed model’s accuracy 0.696 and macro-F1 0.551.
Authors explicitly state results are obtained via classical simulation and frame the work as a methodological case study rather than a demonstration of quantum advantage.

experiments.description: Shallow Transformer encoder over sequences of chunk-level Bloch vectors with CCG type embeddings for the same financial sentiment classification task, trained and evaluated in classical simulation.

algorithm.variant: Transformer encoder over Bloch-vector sequences with CCG type embeddings

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Each chunk Bloch vector rt in R^3 is linearly mapped to a model dimension, concatenated with a CCG type embedding, and combined with positional embeddings before Transformer encoding.
problem_formulation.objective_function: 3-way sentiment classification with class-weighted cross-entropy over Transformer outputs.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Class-specific decision thresholds tuned on the development set.

problem_instance.description: Same Financial PhraseBank 3-class sentiment classification task as the baseline experiment, using chunk-level Bloch-vector sequences as input to a Transformer.
problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Same preprocessing as baseline: CCG chunking, vocabulary rewriting, chunk-boundary preservation, and extraction of Bloch-vector sequences plus type IDs.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Development macro-F1 used for model selection and threshold tuning; test accuracy and macro-F1 reported; attribution statistics also computed on the test set.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Linear projection of Bloch vectors, concatenation with type embeddings, positional embeddings, single-layer 4-head Transformer encoder, masked mean pooling, linear classifier.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Softmax classification; class-specific threshold tuning on dev set; attribution analysis over Bloch, CCG, and type-gate channels.

speedup_claims.caveats: The Transformer stage is entirely classical; no quantum speedup claim is made.

notes: This experiment is entirely classical after Bloch-vector extraction; no QPU or simulator backend is named for the Transformer stage, so hardware.type is not_specified.

The paper does not report a qubit count for the Transformer experiment; the only quantum objects are the per-chunk Bloch vectors from the earlier circuit stage, so num_qubits cannot be directly reported for this experiment.
No asymptotic speedup claim is made.
